title: Is Indoor Air Worse Than Outdoor Air?
h1: Why Is Indoor Air Often Worse Than Outdoor Air?
description: Indoor air can hold more pollutants than outdoor air because they build up with little fresh air to clear them. Learn the common sources and practical fixes.
quick_answer: Often, yes. Pollutants from cooking, cleaning products, furniture, pets, dust and moisture build up indoors because there's limited fresh air to dilute them. That's not always true, though. On wildfire smoke days, outdoor air is usually worse.
body:
Most people think of air pollution as an outdoor problem, but the air inside a home can carry more of some pollutants than the air outside. That's not because homes are dirty. It's because homes are enclosed spaces where everyday activities keep adding particles, gases and moisture, and there's often not enough air exchange to clear them out.

Why does indoor air get polluted?

Pollutants build up indoors for two main reasons: there are lots of sources inside, and not much fresh air to dilute them.

Common indoor sources include:

  • Cooking, especially frying and gas stoves without a vented hood
  • Cleaning products, air fresheners, candles and scented sprays
  • New furniture, flooring, paint and cabinets, which can release chemical vapors
  • Dust, including skin flakes, fabric fibers and tracked-in soil
  • Pets, which add dander and hair
  • Moisture, which can lead to mold and dust mites
  • Combustion appliances, such as gas furnaces, water heaters and fireplaces

Why don't the pollutants just leave?

Most homes rely on natural leaks and open windows for fresh air. When windows stay shut, during hot summers, cold nights, windy days or smoke events, the same air gets recirculated. Your HVAC system moves air around and filters particles, but in most homes it doesn't bring in outdoor air.

Tighter, more efficient homes and remodeled homes with new windows can trap even more. That saves energy, but it means ventilation has to be planned.

Is outdoor air ever worse than indoor air?

Yes. In San Diego County and Orange County, wildfire smoke can make outdoor air far worse than indoor air. Santa Ana winds can also carry heavy dust. On those days, keep windows closed, run your HVAC fan with a good filter and use portable HEPA purifiers. Check local air quality reports before opening up the house.

Homes near busy roads or freeways may also want to be careful about when they bring in outdoor air.

How does indoor air affect health?

For people with allergies, asthma or other breathing issues, poor indoor air can mean more symptoms at home. Common complaints include stuffy noses, itchy eyes, headaches, coughing and trouble sleeping. Symptoms that ease when you leave the house are a clue that indoor air may be a factor.

One serious exception: carbon monoxide from a faulty gas appliance can cause headaches, dizziness and nausea. If you suspect CO, get everyone out and call 911. Keep working CO alarms on every level of the home.

How can I make indoor air cleaner?

The approach is simple: control sources, ventilate and filter.

  1. Control sources. Use fragrance-free cleaners, skip candles and sprays, store paints and solvents in the garage, and fix leaks quickly.
  2. Ventilate. Run the kitchen hood while cooking and bath fans during showers. Open windows when outdoor air is clean.
  3. Filter. Use a pleated filter in your HVAC system, ideally MERV 8 to 13 depending on what your system can handle, and change it on schedule.
  4. Manage humidity. Keep indoor humidity in a moderate range to discourage mold and dust mites.
  5. Clean smart. Vacuum with a HEPA vacuum and dust with a damp cloth.
  6. Consider upgrades. Whole-home purifiers, UV lights for the coil, fresh air ventilation and duct sealing can help when basic steps aren't enough.

Can my HVAC system make indoor air worse?

It can if it's neglected. A clogged filter, a dirty coil, a slimy drain pan or leaky ducts pulling in attic or garage air can all add dust and odors. Regular maintenance, a properly fitted filter and sealed ducts keep the system cleaning the air instead of adding to the problem.

When should I get help?

If someone in your home has ongoing allergy or breathing symptoms, if you notice musty smells, or if dust builds up fast no matter what you do, a professional look can help. A technician can check filtration, airflow, humidity and duct condition to find the weak points.

faqs: What is the biggest source of indoor air pollution?

It varies by home. Common big contributors are cooking without ventilation, cleaning and scented products, moisture and mold, dust and pet dander, and gas appliances. The best fix is to find and reduce the main sources in your own home.
Should I open windows to improve indoor air?

Yes, when outdoor air is clean. A few minutes of cross ventilation can clear a lot of built-up pollutants. Keep windows closed during wildfire smoke, heavy wind-blown dust or high pollen if you're sensitive.
Does my HVAC system bring in fresh air?

Most home systems recirculate indoor air rather than bring in outdoor air. Some homes have a fresh air intake or an energy recovery ventilator. A technician can tell you what your system has and whether adding ventilation makes sense.
Do air purifiers make indoor air cleaner than outside?

A good HEPA purifier can greatly reduce particles in the room where it runs, sometimes making it cleaner than outdoors on bad air days. It doesn't remove gases unless it has a substantial carbon filter, and it doesn't replace ventilation.
